atoms.canonical_statement: The 2018 UKPIN/QPIDS census evaluated the number of immunoglobulin product switches, reactions after switching, treatment delays, and service resource effects.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: questions designed to explore the number of patients affected by the switching of immunoglobulin products

atoms.canonical_statement: The census concerned UK immunodeficiency services managing patients with primary or secondary immunodeficiency receiving immunoglobulin replacement.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: How many primary immunodeficiency (PID) / secondary immunodeficiency (SID) patients on immunoglobulin replacement

population.label: UK immunodeficiency services managing PID/SID patients on immunoglobulin replacement

atoms.canonical_statement: The exposure of interest was switching immunoglobulin products for non-clinical logistical reasons, including commissioning guidance and product withdrawal or shortage.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: switched products as a result of 2017 commissioning guidance

exposures.details: Commissioning guidance, product withdrawal, or shortage

atoms.canonical_statement: Questions on immunoglobulin switching were embedded in the annual UKPIN/QPIDS census and distributed electronically to clinical service leads of registered centres; two unregistered services were contacted directly.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Questions regarding immunoglobulin switching were included in the annual UKPIN/QPIDS census

atoms.canonical_statement: Centres were asked about switch counts, local and systemic reactions, treatment delays, appointment arrangements, displaced nursing activity, and additional hours worked.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The following questions were included in the census electronic questionnaire.

atoms.canonical_statement: Centres reporting reactions were contacted directly to clarify the reaction, hospitalisation, treatment, and outcome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Centres reporting reactions following product switch were contacted directly and details of the reactions were clarified.

atoms.canonical_statement: Retrospective census data were obtained from 33 of 36 UK immunodeficiency centres (92%).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Retrospective census data was collected from 33/36 (92%) UK immunodeficiency centres.

population.label: UK immunodeficiency centres eligible for the census

atoms.canonical_statement: Thirty of 33 responding centres reported that immunoglobulin product switches occurred between July 2017 and May 2018.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Thirty out of thirty-three centres reported that immunoglobulin product switches had occurred

concept.text: Centre reported at least one product switch

atoms.canonical_statement: A total of 802 immunoglobulin product switches were reported.

atoms.canonical_statement: Seventy-nine percent of reported switches were undertaken because of product withdrawal or shortage.

atoms.canonical_statement: Seventeen of 33 services reported that some patients had immunoglobulin infusions delayed because products were unavailable.

atoms.canonical_statement: Five local reactions after product switching were reported by 32 centres answering the question; one centre reported the number as unknown.

atoms.canonical_statement: Seven systemic reactions after product switching were reported by 33 centres answering the question.

atoms.canonical_statement: All four patients with systemic reactions after SC-to-SC switching were managed without hospital admission.

atoms.canonical_statement: One local reaction case after immunoglobulin product switching involved redness and mild itch resolving within hours; chlorpheniramine; product continued with mild symptoms ongoing.

atoms.canonical_statement: One local reaction case after immunoglobulin product switching involved red rash on legs; antihistamines; product continued with no further symptoms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Red rash on legs

atoms.canonical_statement: One local reaction case after immunoglobulin product switching involved local pruritus; antihistamines; new product continued for four months before reverting to original product.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Local pruritus

atoms.canonical_statement: One systemic reaction case after SC-to-SC immunoglobulin switching involved joint and neck pain, headache and stomach ache lasting 1–24 hours; no outpatient treatment; switched to alternative product with no further symptoms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Joint and neck pain, headache and stomach ache

concept.text: Joint and neck pain, headache and stomach ache

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Joint and neck pain, headache and stomach ache

atoms.canonical_statement: One systemic reaction case after SC-to-SC immunoglobulin switching involved dizziness described as “swimming in head” and fatigue lasting up to 7 days; no objective symptom on observed infusion; switched to alternative product with no further symptoms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dizziness and fatigue

atoms.canonical_statement: One systemic reaction case after SC-to-SC immunoglobulin switching involved headache, malaise, abdominal pain and painful skin rash; treated with paracetamol, antihistamines and 3 days of prednisolone; switched back to previous product.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Headache, malaise, abdominal pain and skin rash

concept.text: Headache, malaise, abdominal pain and skin rash

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Headache, malaise, abdominal pain and skin rash

atoms.canonical_statement: One systemic reaction case after SC-to-SC immunoglobulin switching involved palpitations during infusion followed two weeks later by a widespread raised rash; treated with cetirizine; switched to an alternative product and rash resolved.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Palpitations and delayed widespread rash

atoms.canonical_statement: One systemic reaction case after IV-to-IV immunoglobulin switching involved fever, headache and flu-like illness with shaking beginning the evening of infusion and lasting 1–2 days; no treatment; switched to alternative IV product.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fever, headache and flu-like illness

atoms.canonical_statement: One systemic reaction case after IV-to-IV immunoglobulin switching involved severe back pain one hour after leaving clinic; attended the emergency department, received analgesia and was discharged; fatigue and back pain continued for a couple of days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Severe back pain

atoms.canonical_statement: One systemic reaction case after IV-to-IV immunoglobulin switching involved patient with longstanding intolerance of multiple products reported next-day tiredness with joint and muscle pains; no treatment; switched back to original product.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study relied on retrospective recollection by immunology teams for the number of reactions experienced by patients.

atoms.canonical_statement: The census did not collect data on improvement of pre-existing mild local reactions after switching.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Data regarding improvement of symptoms following switching were not collected in this census.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the census as suggesting more flexibility in switching arrangements than previously thought, particularly for SC-to-SC switches.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: It suggests that there may be more flexibility regarding arrangements for product switching than previously thought

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that immunoglobulin product switches are feasible in patients with primary immunodeficiency when switching is necessary.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: these data provide evidence that product switches are feasible in patients with primary immunodeficiency
